Robust, arbitrary-precision evaluation of the two Meijer-G shapes this package needs.

Source: R/meijer.R
meijer-overview.Rd

Every closed form in the paper is one of exactly two restricted Meijer-G shapes (confirmed by inspecting every call site in the Python original, background._f_N_scalar and statfactor._B_scalar):

Details

  G^{N,0}_{0,N}(z | -- ; b_1,...,b_N)   (gamma chain,        s = 1/2)
  G^{0,N}_{N,0}(z | b_1,...,b_N ; --)   (inverse-gamma chain, s = 1)

Both are "numerator-empty"/"denominator-empty" cases of the general Meijer G, which is why they admit a closed-form reduction to a finite sum of generalized hypergeometric terms rather than needing a black-box Mellin-Barnes routine (R has no arbitrary-precision complex arithmetic – Rmpfr wraps MPFR, real only – which is the concrete reason contour quadrature was rejected as the implementation strategy; see the plan).

Derivation (residue sum of the Mellin-Barnes integral, closing the contour at the simple poles of each Gamma(b_j + s)): for pairwise-distinct b_i,

  G^{N,0}_{0,N}(z|--;b) = sum_j  z^{b_j} * prod_{i!=j} Gamma(b_i - b_j)
                               * 0F_{N-1}(--; {1+b_j-b_i}_{i!=j}; (-1)^N z)

Verified by hand against two independent, oracle-free identities already pinned in the Python test suite (tests/test_meijer.py):

  N=1: reduces to z^{b_1} e^{-z}  (matches G^{1,0}_{0,1}(z|--;0) = e^{-z})
  N=2: reduces to 2 z^{a/2} K_a(2 sqrt(z))  (the b=(a,0) Bessel-K identity)

Both reductions are worked out in full in docs/meijer_derivation.md.

The mirror shape needs no separate derivation: substituting s -> -s in its own Mellin-Barnes integral gives

  G^{0,N}_{N,0}(z|b;--) = G^{N,0}_{0,N}(1/z|--;1-b)

directly (this is DLMF 16.19.1 specialized to p=m=0), so only one routine (.g_core) is implemented and hardened.
